| Spouses | Rosario Varela ​ (divorced)​ * Melissa Thomas |
| Children | 4 |

**David Koepp** (;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-1) born June 9, 1963) is an American screenwriter and director. As of February 2026, he is the fourth most successful screenwriter of all time in terms of U.S. box office receipts with a total gross of over $2.97 billion.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-2)

Koepp is known for a variety of screenplays, including those of the [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg")–directed films _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park "Jurassic Park")_ (1993), _[The Lost World: Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_World:\_Jurassic\_Park "The Lost World: Jurassic Park")_ (1997), _[War of the Worlds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War\_of\_the\_Worlds\_(2005\_film) "War of the Worlds (2005 film)")_ (2005), _[Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones\_and\_the\_Kingdom\_of\_the\_Crystal\_Skull "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull")_ (2008) and _[Disclosure Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disclosure\_Day "Disclosure Day")_ (2026). Other Koepp screenplays include those for the crime film _[Carlito's Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlito's\_Way "Carlito's Way")_ (1993); the action spy films _[Mission: Impossible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission:\_Impossible\_(film) "Mission: Impossible (film)")_ (1996) and _[Jack Ryan: Shadow Recruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack\_Ryan:\_Shadow\_Recruit "Jack Ryan: Shadow Recruit")_ (2014); the superhero film _[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_(2002\_film) "Spider-Man (2002 film)")_ (2002); another _[Indiana Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones "Indiana Jones")_ film, _[The Dial of Destiny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones\_and\_the\_Dial\_of\_Destiny "Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny")_ (2023); and another _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(franchise) "Jurassic Park (franchise)")_ film, _[Jurassic World Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World\_Rebirth "Jurassic World Rebirth")_ (2025).

Koepp has also directed seven feature films: _[The Trigger Effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Trigger\_Effect "The Trigger Effect")_ (1996), _[Stir of Echoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stir\_of\_Echoes "Stir of Echoes")_ (1999), _[Secret Window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Window "Secret Window")_ (2004), _[Ghost Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Town\_(2008\_film) "Ghost Town (2008 film)")_ (2008), _[Premium Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium\_Rush "Premium Rush")_ (2012), _[Mortdecai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortdecai\_(film) "Mortdecai (film)")_ (2015), and _[You Should Have Left](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Should\_Have\_Left "You Should Have Left")_ (2020).

Koepp was born in [Pewaukee, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pewaukee,_Wisconsin "Pewaukee, Wisconsin"), as the youngest of four children to Margaret (Fairfield), a family therapist, and Donald Koepp, who owned a [billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_(advertising) "Billboard (advertising)") company.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-LATimes1994-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-6)

Originally studying to become an actor, first at the [University of Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Minnesota "University of Minnesota") for one year and afterwards at the [University of Wisconsin–Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Wisconsin%E2%80%93Madison "University of Wisconsin–Madison") for two years, he enrolled in the film school of the [University of California, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles "University of California, Los Angeles"), in 1984.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-LATimes1994-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-8) He graduated with a bachelor's degree in film from UCLA in 1990.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-9)

As a writer, Koepp worked on blockbuster [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_(film_industry) "Hollywood (film industry)") films such as _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(film) "Jurassic Park (film)")_ with [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg"), _[Mission: Impossible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission:\_Impossible\_(film) "Mission: Impossible (film)")_ with [Brian De Palma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_De_Palma "Brian De Palma") and _[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_(2002\_film) "Spider-Man (2002 film)")_ with [Sam Raimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi "Sam Raimi").

Koepp had a [cameo appearance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_appearance "Cameo appearance") as the "Unlucky Bastard", a minor character devoured by a _[T. rex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrannosaurus "Tyrannosaurus")_ that roams [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego") in _[The Lost World: Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_World:\_Jurassic\_Park "The Lost World: Jurassic Park")_, which he co-wrote and for which he was a second unit director. Although Koepp did not write _[Jurassic Park III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_III "Jurassic Park III")_, he did devise the film's basic storyline.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-11) Koepp later declined an offer to write a script for the fourth film in the series, _[Jurassic World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World "Jurassic World")_, as he felt he had nothing left to contribute to the series.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-12)

Koepp was reportedly paid $4,000,000 for his _[Panic Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic\_Room\_(film) "Panic Room (film)")_ screenplay. He wrote the screenplay for _[Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones\_and\_the\_Kingdom\_of\_the\_Crystal\_Skull "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull")_ for [Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg") and [George Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Lucas "George Lucas") and co-wrote and directed 2008's _[Ghost Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Town\_(2008\_film) "Ghost Town (2008 film)")_ starring [Ricky Gervais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Gervais "Ricky Gervais") and [Greg Kinnear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kinnear "Greg Kinnear").

Koepp's work as a director has not had quite the same box office success. His films include _[Secret Window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Window "Secret Window")_, _[Stir of Echoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stir\_of\_Echoes "Stir of Echoes")_, and _[The Trigger Effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Trigger\_Effect "The Trigger Effect")_. Koepp has worked in television, creating the 2002 series _[Hack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hack\_(TV\_series) "Hack (TV series)")_ starring [David Morse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Morse_(actor) "David Morse (actor)").

In 2012, Koepp directed _[Premium Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium\_Rush "Premium Rush")_, which he co-wrote with John Kamps.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-13) In an August 2011 lawsuit, [Joe Quirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Quirk "Joe Quirk"), the author of the 1998 novel _[The Ultimate Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ultimate\_Rush "The Ultimate Rush")_, accused Koepp and the makers of _Premium Rush_ of copyright infringement.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-14) On April 2, 2013, [U.S. District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_District?action=edit&redlink=1 "United States District (page does not exist)") Judge [Richard Seeborg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Seeborg "Richard Seeborg") dismissed this case, finding that the two works were not substantially similar.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-15)

On February 17, 2013, Koepp received the WGA East's Ian McClellan Hunter Award for Career Achievement.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-16)

On July 10, 2013, [Lionsgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionsgate_Films "Lionsgate Films") was reported to have acquired the comedic crime novel _The Great Mortdecai Moustache Mystery_, written by [Kyril Bonfiglioli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyril_Bonfiglioli "Kyril Bonfiglioli").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-17) Koepp directed the film, titled _[Mortdecai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortdecai\_(film) "Mortdecai (film)")_, from a script by Eric Aronson.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-18)[Johnny Depp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Depp "Johnny Depp") played the lead role of Charlie Mortdecai,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-19) and the film also featured [Gwyneth Paltrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwyneth_Paltrow "Gwyneth Paltrow"), [Ewan McGregor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewan_McGregor "Ewan McGregor"), and [Paul Bettany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Bettany "Paul Bettany").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-20) Koepp adapted the [Marcus Sakey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Sakey "Marcus Sakey") novel _Brilliance_, which will star [Will Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Smith "Will Smith") and [Noomi Rapace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noomi_Rapace "Noomi Rapace").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-21)

On March 15, 2016, [The Walt Disney Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") announced [a fifth installment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Jones_and_the_Dial_of_Destiny "Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny") of the _[Indiana Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones "Indiana Jones")_ saga, with Koepp as its screenwriter and [Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg") directing again.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-23) By June 2018, Koepp ultimately backed out of the project due to his commitment to _[You Should Have Left](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Should\_Have\_Left "You Should Have Left")_, a horror drama film Koepp wrote and directed.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-24) Based on the novel of the same name by [Daniel Kehlmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Kehlmann "Daniel Kehlmann"), _You Should Have Left_ was released in 2020, and stars [Kevin Bacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Bacon "Kevin Bacon") and [Amanda Seyfried](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Seyfried "Amanda Seyfried").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-26)

On September 3, 2019, Koepp made his novel debut with the publication of _Cold Storage_, a science-fiction thriller.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-27) A [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_Storage_(film) "Cold Storage (film)") was announced in May 2022 from [Studiocanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studiocanal "Studiocanal"), with Koepp writing the screenplay and [Jonny Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonny_Campbell "Jonny Campbell") directing; the cast consists of [Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson"), [Joe Keery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Keery "Joe Keery"), [Georgina Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgina_Campbell "Georgina Campbell"), and [Sosie Bacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sosie_Bacon "Sosie Bacon").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-29)

On December 10, 2020, [Amasia Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amasia_Entertainment "Amasia Entertainment") and [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures") announced Koepp had been tapped to write the script for a reboot of the [Green Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Hornet "Green Hornet") franchise titled _The Green Hornet and Kato_.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-30) On February 25, 2021, it was announced Koepp would write and co-produce the thriller _[Kimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi\_(film) "Kimi (film)")_, directed by [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh") and starring [Zoë Kravitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zo%C3%AB_Kravitz "Zoë Kravitz").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-31) The film was released on [Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_(streaming_service) "Max (streaming service)") (then HBO Max) on February 10, 2022.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-32)

Koepp's second novel _Aurora_ was published on June 7, 2022, and a film adaptation of the book is in development for [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix"), with Koepp writing the script and [Kathryn Bigelow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathryn_Bigelow "Kathryn Bigelow") directing.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-33)

Koepp wrote the screenplay for the psychological thriller film _[Presence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presence\_(2024\_film) "Presence (2024 film)")_, which was directed by Soderbergh and premiered at the [2024 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Sundance_Film_Festival "2024 Sundance Film Festival").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-34) Koepp would reunite with Soderbergh on spy film _[Black Bag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Bag "Black Bag")_, which was released in theatres on March 14, 2025 by [Focus Features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_Features "Focus Features").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-36) On January 22, 2024, it was announced that Koepp would return to the _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(franchise) "Jurassic Park (franchise)")_ franchise by writing _[Jurassic World Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World\_Rebirth "Jurassic World Rebirth")_, with [Gareth Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Edwards_(filmmaker) "Gareth Edwards (filmmaker)") directing and Spielberg serving as executive producer.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-38) In April 2024, it was confirmed that Koepp and Spielberg would work again on an original film about [UFOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unidentified_flying_object "Unidentified flying object"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-40) later revealed to be titled _[Disclosure Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disclosure\_Day "Disclosure Day")_ with a planned June 2026 release.[[41]](

| Born | June 9, 1963 (age 63) [Pewaukee, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pewaukee,_Wisconsin "Pewaukee, Wisconsin"), U.S. |
| Education | [University of Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Minnesota "University of Minnesota") (attended) [University of Wisconsin, Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Wisconsin,_Madison "University of Wisconsin, Madison") (attended) [University of California, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles "University of California, Los Angeles") ([BFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Fine_Arts "Bachelor of Fine Arts")) |
| Occupations | * Screenwriter * director * author |
| Years active | 1988–present |

| Spouses | Rosario Varela ​ (divorced)​ * Melissa Thomas |
| Children | 4 |

**David Koepp** (;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-1) born June 9, 1963) is an American screenwriter and director. As of February 2026, he is the fourth most successful screenwriter of all time in terms of U.S. box office receipts with a total gross of over $2.97 billion.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-2)

Koepp is known for a variety of screenplays, including those of the [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg")–directed films _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park "Jurassic Park")_ (1993), _[The Lost World: Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_World:\_Jurassic\_Park "The Lost World: Jurassic Park")_ (1997), _[War of the Worlds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War\_of\_the\_Worlds\_(2005\_film) "War of the Worlds (2005 film)")_ (2005), _[Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones\_and\_the\_Kingdom\_of\_the\_Crystal\_Skull "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull")_ (2008) and _[Disclosure Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disclosure\_Day "Disclosure Day")_ (2026). Other Koepp screenplays include those for the crime film _[Carlito's Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlito's\_Way "Carlito's Way")_ (1993); the action spy films _[Mission: Impossible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission:\_Impossible\_(film) "Mission: Impossible (film)")_ (1996) and _[Jack Ryan: Shadow Recruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack\_Ryan:\_Shadow\_Recruit "Jack Ryan: Shadow Recruit")_ (2014); the superhero film _[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_(2002\_film) "Spider-Man (2002 film)")_ (2002); another _[Indiana Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones "Indiana Jones")_ film, _[The Dial of Destiny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones\_and\_the\_Dial\_of\_Destiny "Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny")_ (2023); and another _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(franchise) "Jurassic Park (franchise)")_ film, _[Jurassic World Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World\_Rebirth "Jurassic World Rebirth")_ (2025).

Koepp has also directed seven feature films: _[The Trigger Effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Trigger\_Effect "The Trigger Effect")_ (1996), _[Stir of Echoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stir\_of\_Echoes "Stir of Echoes")_ (1999), _[Secret Window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Window "Secret Window")_ (2004), _[Ghost Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Town\_(2008\_film) "Ghost Town (2008 film)")_ (2008), _[Premium Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium\_Rush "Premium Rush")_ (2012), _[Mortdecai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortdecai\_(film) "Mortdecai (film)")_ (2015), and _[You Should Have Left](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Should\_Have\_Left "You Should Have Left")_ (2020).

Koepp was born in [Pewaukee, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pewaukee,_Wisconsin "Pewaukee, Wisconsin"), as the youngest of four children to Margaret (Fairfield), a family therapist, and Donald Koepp, who owned a [billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_(advertising) "Billboard (advertising)") company.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-LATimes1994-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-6)

Originally studying to become an actor, first at the [University of Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Minnesota "University of Minnesota") for one year and afterwards at the [University of Wisconsin–Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Wisconsin%E2%80%93Madison "University of Wisconsin–Madison") for two years, he enrolled in the film school of the [University of California, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Los_Angeles "University of California, Los Angeles"), in 1984.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-LATimes1994-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-8) He graduated with a bachelor's degree in film from UCLA in 1990.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-9)

As a writer, Koepp worked on blockbuster [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_(film_industry) "Hollywood (film industry)") films such as _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(film) "Jurassic Park (film)")_ with [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg"), _[Mission: Impossible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission:\_Impossible\_(film) "Mission: Impossible (film)")_ with [Brian De Palma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_De_Palma "Brian De Palma") and _[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_(2002\_film) "Spider-Man (2002 film)")_ with [Sam Raimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi "Sam Raimi").

Koepp had a [cameo appearance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_appearance "Cameo appearance") as the "Unlucky Bastard", a minor character devoured by a _[T. rex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrannosaurus "Tyrannosaurus")_ that roams [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego") in _[The Lost World: Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_World:\_Jurassic\_Park "The Lost World: Jurassic Park")_, which he co-wrote and for which he was a second unit director. Although Koepp did not write _[Jurassic Park III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_III "Jurassic Park III")_, he did devise the film's basic storyline.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-11) Koepp later declined an offer to write a script for the fourth film in the series, _[Jurassic World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World "Jurassic World")_, as he felt he had nothing left to contribute to the series.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-12)

Koepp was reportedly paid $4,000,000 for his _[Panic Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic\_Room\_(film) "Panic Room (film)")_ screenplay. He wrote the screenplay for _[Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones\_and\_the\_Kingdom\_of\_the\_Crystal\_Skull "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull")_ for [Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg") and [George Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Lucas "George Lucas") and co-wrote and directed 2008's _[Ghost Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Town\_(2008\_film) "Ghost Town (2008 film)")_ starring [Ricky Gervais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Gervais "Ricky Gervais") and [Greg Kinnear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kinnear "Greg Kinnear").

Koepp's work as a director has not had quite the same box office success. His films include _[Secret Window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Window "Secret Window")_, _[Stir of Echoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stir\_of\_Echoes "Stir of Echoes")_, and _[The Trigger Effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Trigger\_Effect "The Trigger Effect")_. Koepp has worked in television, creating the 2002 series _[Hack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hack\_(TV\_series) "Hack (TV series)")_ starring [David Morse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Morse_(actor) "David Morse (actor)").

In 2012, Koepp directed _[Premium Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium\_Rush "Premium Rush")_, which he co-wrote with John Kamps.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-13) In an August 2011 lawsuit, [Joe Quirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Quirk "Joe Quirk"), the author of the 1998 novel _[The Ultimate Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ultimate\_Rush "The Ultimate Rush")_, accused Koepp and the makers of _Premium Rush_ of copyright infringement.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-14) On April 2, 2013, [U.S. District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_District?action=edit&redlink=1 "United States District (page does not exist)") Judge [Richard Seeborg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Seeborg "Richard Seeborg") dismissed this case, finding that the two works were not substantially similar.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-15)

On February 17, 2013, Koepp received the WGA East's Ian McClellan Hunter Award for Career Achievement.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-16)

On July 10, 2013, [Lionsgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionsgate_Films "Lionsgate Films") was reported to have acquired the comedic crime novel _The Great Mortdecai Moustache Mystery_, written by [Kyril Bonfiglioli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyril_Bonfiglioli "Kyril Bonfiglioli").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-17) Koepp directed the film, titled _[Mortdecai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortdecai\_(film) "Mortdecai (film)")_, from a script by Eric Aronson.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-18)[Johnny Depp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Depp "Johnny Depp") played the lead role of Charlie Mortdecai,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-19) and the film also featured [Gwyneth Paltrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwyneth_Paltrow "Gwyneth Paltrow"), [Ewan McGregor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewan_McGregor "Ewan McGregor"), and [Paul Bettany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Bettany "Paul Bettany").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-20) Koepp adapted the [Marcus Sakey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Sakey "Marcus Sakey") novel _Brilliance_, which will star [Will Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Smith "Will Smith") and [Noomi Rapace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noomi_Rapace "Noomi Rapace").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-21)

On March 15, 2016, [The Walt Disney Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") announced [a fifth installment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Jones_and_the_Dial_of_Destiny "Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny") of the _[Indiana Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones "Indiana Jones")_ saga, with Koepp as its screenwriter and [Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg") directing again.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-23) By June 2018, Koepp ultimately backed out of the project due to his commitment to _[You Should Have Left](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Should\_Have\_Left "You Should Have Left")_, a horror drama film Koepp wrote and directed.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-24) Based on the novel of the same name by [Daniel Kehlmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Kehlmann "Daniel Kehlmann"), _You Should Have Left_ was released in 2020, and stars [Kevin Bacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Bacon "Kevin Bacon") and [Amanda Seyfried](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Seyfried "Amanda Seyfried").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-26)

On September 3, 2019, Koepp made his novel debut with the publication of _Cold Storage_, a science-fiction thriller.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-27) A [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_Storage_(film) "Cold Storage (film)") was announced in May 2022 from [Studiocanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studiocanal "Studiocanal"), with Koepp writing the screenplay and [Jonny Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonny_Campbell "Jonny Campbell") directing; the cast consists of [Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson"), [Joe Keery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Keery "Joe Keery"), [Georgina Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgina_Campbell "Georgina Campbell"), and [Sosie Bacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sosie_Bacon "Sosie Bacon").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-29)

On December 10, 2020, [Amasia Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amasia_Entertainment "Amasia Entertainment") and [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures") announced Koepp had been tapped to write the script for a reboot of the [Green Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Hornet "Green Hornet") franchise titled _The Green Hornet and Kato_.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-30) On February 25, 2021, it was announced Koepp would write and co-produce the thriller _[Kimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi\_(film) "Kimi (film)")_, directed by [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh") and starring [Zoë Kravitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zo%C3%AB_Kravitz "Zoë Kravitz").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-31) The film was released on [Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_(streaming_service) "Max (streaming service)") (then HBO Max) on February 10, 2022.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-32)

Koepp's second novel _Aurora_ was published on June 7, 2022, and a film adaptation of the book is in development for [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix"), with Koepp writing the script and [Kathryn Bigelow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathryn_Bigelow "Kathryn Bigelow") directing.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-33)

Koepp wrote the screenplay for the psychological thriller film _[Presence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presence\_(2024\_film) "Presence (2024 film)")_, which was directed by Soderbergh and premiered at the [2024 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Sundance_Film_Festival "2024 Sundance Film Festival").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-34) Koepp would reunite with Soderbergh on spy film _[Black Bag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Bag "Black Bag")_, which was released in theatres on March 14, 2025 by [Focus Features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_Features "Focus Features").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-36) On January 22, 2024, it was announced that Koepp would return to the _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(franchise) "Jurassic Park (franchise)")_ franchise by writing _[Jurassic World Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_World\_Rebirth "Jurassic World Rebirth")_, with [Gareth Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Edwards_(filmmaker) "Gareth Edwards (filmmaker)") directing and Spielberg serving as executive producer.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-38) In April 2024, it was confirmed that Koepp and Spielberg would work again on an original film about [UFOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unidentified_flying_object "Unidentified flying object"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp#cite_note-40) later revealed to be titled _[Disclosure Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disclosure\_Day "Disclosure Day")_ with a planned June 2026 release.[[41]](

**William Condon** (born October 22, 1955) is an American director and screenwriter. Condon is known for writing and/or directing numerous successful and acclaimed films including _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_, _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_1 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1")_, _[Part 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_2 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2")_, and _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(2017\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-CondonDisneylive-actionBeautyandtheBeast-1) He has received two nominations for the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay"), _Gods and Monsters_ and _Chicago_, winning for the former.

Condon was born in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") on October 22, 1955,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-ibdb-2) the son of a police [detective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detective "Detective"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-3) and was raised in an [Irish Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Catholic "Irish Catholic") family.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-5) He attended [Regis High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regis_High_School_(New_York_City) "Regis High School (New York City)") and [Columbia College of Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_College_of_Columbia_University "Columbia College of Columbia University"), graduating in 1976 with a degree in philosophy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)
Two films had a significant impact of Condon's early life. At the age of twelve, he found himself drawn to screenplay writing with his first viewing of [_Bonnie and Clyde_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_and_Clyde_(film) "Bonnie and Clyde (film)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-6) In college he saw _[Sweet Charity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet\_Charity\_(film) "Sweet Charity (film)")_ (1969), which led to "a lifelong love affair with movies that are reviled and rejected in their time."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)

After completing college, Condon worked as a journalist for film magazines, including _[American Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Film\_(magazine) "American Film (magazine)")_ and _Millimeter_. In 1981, he won "the world's most difficult film trivia quiz" sponsored by _[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Village\_Voice "The Village Voice")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-7)
His career as a filmmaker began with screenplays for the [independent feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_film "Independent film")_[Strange Behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strange\_Behavior "Strange Behavior")_ (1981), an homage to the pulp horror films of the 1950s,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-sb-8) and the [science-fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science-fiction "Science-fiction") feature _[Strange Invaders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strange\_Invaders "Strange Invaders")_ (1983), which starred [Nancy Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Allen_(actress) "Nancy Allen (actress)") and [Wallace Shawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallace_Shawn "Wallace Shawn").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-9)
His directorial debut was _[Sister, Sister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister,\_Sister\_(1987\_film) "Sister, Sister (1987 film)")_ (1987), an eerie [Southern Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Gothic "Southern Gothic") mystery starring [Eric Stoltz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Stoltz "Eric Stoltz") and [Jennifer Jason Leigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Jason_Leigh "Jennifer Jason Leigh"). Test screenings led to major changes to the film, which still proved a critical failure that set back Condon's career.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-10)

Condon emerged a few years later directing a series of made-for-TV thrillers, including _[Murder 101](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder\_101\_(1991\_film) "Murder 101 (1991 film)")_ (1991), which earned Condon and co-writer Roy Johansen a 1992 [Edgar Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Award "Edgar Award") for their screenplay.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-mysterynet-11) During this period he also wrote the screenplay for the thriller _[F/X2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/X2 "F/X2")_ (1991), which was directed by Australian director [Richard Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Franklin_(director) "Richard Franklin (director)").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-12)
In 1994, he directed the television movie _[The Man Who Wouldn't Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Man\_Who\_Wouldn't\_Die\_(1995\_film) "The Man Who Wouldn't Die (1995 film)"),_ which was met with mixed reviews.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-13) He directed _[Candyman: Farewell to the Flesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candyman:\_Farewell\_to\_the\_Flesh "Candyman: Farewell to the Flesh")_ (1995), a sequel to [Bernard Rose's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Rose_(director) "Bernard Rose (director)") 1992 horror film. It was a critical and commercial failure.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-14) Reminded years later of this phase of his career, Condon said: "It's hard to be lower on the totem pole than being the director for a sequel to a horror movie."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)

Condon wrote and directed _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_ (1998), which was based on a novel by [Christopher Bram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Bram "Christopher Bram"). His screenplay won the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Writing_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Writing Adapted Screenplay"). _The New York Times_ said Condon "may have been the most stunned person at the Academy Awards when his name was announced as the winner for the best adapted screenplay. He has struggled for years in Hollywood as a screenwriter and journalist and is unaccustomed to the hoopla that is now around him."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-15) He was nominated for the same award for his screenplay for _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, based on the Broadway musical of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_(musical) "Chicago (musical)").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-16) He received a second Edgar Award for his _Chicago_ screenplay as well.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-17)

In 2004 he wrote and directed the film _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, chronicling the life of the controversial sex researcher [Alfred Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey "Alfred Kinsey"). In _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, [A.O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.O._Scott "A.O. Scott") wrote that "Bill Condon's smart, stirring [film] has a lot to say on the subject of sex, which it treats with sobriety, sensitivity and a welcome measure of humor." He continued: "I can't think of another movie that has dealt with sex so knowledgeably and, at the same time, made the pursuit of knowledge seem so sexy. There are some explicit images and provocative scenes, but it is your intellect that is most likely to be aroused.... Mr. Condon's great achievement is to turn Kinsey's complicated and controversial career into a grand intellectual drama."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-18)
In 2005, he received the [Stephen F. Kolzak Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD_Media_Awards "GLAAD Media Awards") at the [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD "GLAAD") Media Awards.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-19)
Condon wrote the screenplay for and directed _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, an adaptation of the acclaimed Broadway musical of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls "Dreamgirls"). It was released in December 2006. Condon received [Directors Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America "Directors Guild of America") and [Broadcast Film Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_Film_Critics_Association "Broadcast Film Critics Association") nominations for directing. The film was nominated for eight Academy Awards in six categories.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-20)

Condon was executive producer of the [81st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards") television broadcast that aired on February 22, 2009, working with producer [Laurence Mark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Mark "Laurence Mark").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-21)
Condon directed both parts of _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaking\_Dawn\_(disambiguation) "Breaking Dawn (disambiguation)")_ (2011 and 2012), adapted from the fourth and final novel in _[The Twilight Saga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_(novel\_series) "Twilight (novel series)")_ by [Stephenie Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephenie_Meyer "Stephenie Meyer"). He was twice nominated for a [Razzie for Worst Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Award_for_Worst_Director "Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Director") for these films, winning for _Part 2_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-22)
Condon directed _[The Fifth Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fifth\_Estate\_(film) "The Fifth Estate (film)")_ (2013), a thriller about [WikiLeaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks "WikiLeaks") starring [Benedict Cumberbatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_Cumberbatch "Benedict Cumberbatch"). He said he chose the project for a change of pace and liked its non-ideological approach to a very complex subject. He saw it "in the great tradition of journalistic thrillers".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-23) It received mixed responses from critics and underperformed at the box office.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-24)

In late 2013, he directed a revised version of the 1997 stage musical _[Side Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side\_Show\_(musical) "Side Show (musical)")_ at the [La Jolla Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Jolla_Playhouse "La Jolla Playhouse"). A production of this revision played in June and July 2014 at the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center"). [Charles Isherwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Isherwood "Charles Isherwood") described it in _The New York Times_ as "a full-scale reimagining" of the musical that involved "the addition and subtraction of several songs ..., the reordering of others", and new dialogue contributed by Condon.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-25) That production received excellent reviews when it moved to Broadway in the fall, but it proved a failure at the box office and closed after just seven weeks.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-26)
In 2015, Condon directed _[Mr. Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_Holmes "Mr. Holmes")_ starring [Ian McKellen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_McKellen "Ian McKellen"). Condon noted its similarity to _Gods and Monsters_, not only because of its lead actor but because "[b]oth movies are about aging and mortality. You have a celebrated man facing the decline of his public image."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-27)

Condon directed the 2017 [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures")'s [live action film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_and_the_Beast_(2017_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)"), [based on](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_remakes_and_adaptations_of_Disney_animated_films "List of remakes and adaptations of Disney animated films") the animated 1991 film _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(1991\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (1991 film)")_, starring [Emma Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Watson "Emma Watson") and [Dan Stevens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Stevens "Dan Stevens").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-CondonDisneylive-actionBeautyandtheBeast-1) A few weeks before the film's scheduled release on March 17, 2017, Condon announced that one character, LeFou, has "a nice, exclusively gay moment", which resulted in an "internet meltdown" of contrasting support and condemnation.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-28)
He co-authored the screenplay for _[The Greatest Showman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Greatest\_Showman "The Greatest Showman")_, a biography of [P.T. Barnum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P.T._Barnum "P.T. Barnum"), starring [Hugh Jackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Jackman "Hugh Jackman") and released in December 2017. He rewrote the draft of co-author [Jenny Bicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenny_Bicks "Jenny Bicks").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-29)

In October 2017, Condon postponed pre-production of a remake of _[Bride of Frankenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bride\_of\_Frankenstein#Remake\_attempts "Bride of Frankenstein")_ for [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures"). _[Deadline Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline\_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")_ reported that Condon and [David Koepp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp "David Koepp") wanted to rework the script.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-30)
Condon is a member of the Independent Feature Projects (IFP) in Los Angeles, a non-profit organization which supports independent films, as well as the Independent Writers Steering Committee, which was initiated by the Writers Guild of America (WGA).
In July 2021, Condon signed on to direct a _[Guys and Dolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guys\_and\_Dolls "Guys and Dolls")_ movie adaptation by [TriStar Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TriStar_Pictures "TriStar Pictures") but left the project in 2023 and was replaced by _Chicago_ director [Rob Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Marshall "Rob Marshall").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-31) That same year, he co-produced the [live stage filming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_from_Away_(film) "Come from Away (film)") of the Broadway production of _[Come from Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come\_from\_Away "Come from Away")_, which was released to streaming on [Apple TV+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV+ "Apple TV+").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-32)

In December 2023, it was announced that Condon would write and direct a [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(2025_film) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (2025 film)") of the [musical version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(musical) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (musical)") of _[Kiss of the Spider Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss\_of\_the\_Spider\_Woman\_(novel) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (novel)")_, with [Jennifer Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lopez "Jennifer Lopez") attached to star and co-executive produce.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-33)
In July 2026, it was revealed that Condon was filming his next film, _The Road Home_, in South Africa. It is about [Hugh Masekela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Masekela "Hugh Masekela") and the conflict he faced from recording with [Paul Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Simon "Paul Simon") during [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-34)
Condon is [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-35) He is in a long-term relationship with Jack Morrissey.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-budget-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-37)

**William Condon** (born October 22, 1955) is an American director and screenwriter. Condon is known for writing and/or directing numerous successful and acclaimed films including _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_, _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_1 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1")_, _[Part 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_2 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2")_, and _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(2017\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-CondonDisneylive-actionBeautyandtheBeast-1) He has received two nominations for the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay"), _Gods and Monsters_ and _Chicago_, winning for the former.

Condon was born in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") on October 22, 1955,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-ibdb-2) the son of a police [detective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detective "Detective"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-3) and was raised in an [Irish Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Catholic "Irish Catholic") family.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-5) He attended [Regis High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regis_High_School_(New_York_City) "Regis High School (New York City)") and [Columbia College of Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_College_of_Columbia_University "Columbia College of Columbia University"), graduating in 1976 with a degree in philosophy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)
Two films had a significant impact of Condon's early life. At the age of twelve, he found himself drawn to screenplay writing with his first viewing of [_Bonnie and Clyde_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_and_Clyde_(film) "Bonnie and Clyde (film)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-6) In college he saw _[Sweet Charity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet\_Charity\_(film) "Sweet Charity (film)")_ (1969), which led to "a lifelong love affair with movies that are reviled and rejected in their time."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)

After completing college, Condon worked as a journalist for film magazines, including _[American Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Film\_(magazine) "American Film (magazine)")_ and _Millimeter_. In 1981, he won "the world's most difficult film trivia quiz" sponsored by _[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Village\_Voice "The Village Voice")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-7)
His career as a filmmaker began with screenplays for the [independent feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_film "Independent film")_[Strange Behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strange\_Behavior "Strange Behavior")_ (1981), an homage to the pulp horror films of the 1950s,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-sb-8) and the [science-fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science-fiction "Science-fiction") feature _[Strange Invaders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strange\_Invaders "Strange Invaders")_ (1983), which starred [Nancy Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Allen_(actress) "Nancy Allen (actress)") and [Wallace Shawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallace_Shawn "Wallace Shawn").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-9)
His directorial debut was _[Sister, Sister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister,\_Sister\_(1987\_film) "Sister, Sister (1987 film)")_ (1987), an eerie [Southern Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Gothic "Southern Gothic") mystery starring [Eric Stoltz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Stoltz "Eric Stoltz") and [Jennifer Jason Leigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Jason_Leigh "Jennifer Jason Leigh"). Test screenings led to major changes to the film, which still proved a critical failure that set back Condon's career.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-10)

Condon emerged a few years later directing a series of made-for-TV thrillers, including _[Murder 101](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder\_101\_(1991\_film) "Murder 101 (1991 film)")_ (1991), which earned Condon and co-writer Roy Johansen a 1992 [Edgar Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Award "Edgar Award") for their screenplay.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-mysterynet-11) During this period he also wrote the screenplay for the thriller _[F/X2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/X2 "F/X2")_ (1991), which was directed by Australian director [Richard Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Franklin_(director) "Richard Franklin (director)").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-12)

In _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, [A.O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.O._Scott "A.O. Scott") wrote that "Bill Condon's smart, stirring [film] has a lot to say on the subject of sex, which it treats with sobriety, sensitivity and a welcome measure of humor." In late 2013, he directed a revised version of the 1997 stage musical _[Side Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side\_Show\_(musical) "Side Show (musical)")_ at the [La Jolla Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Jolla_Playhouse "La Jolla Playhouse"). A production of this revision played in June and July 2014 at the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center"). [Charles Isherwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Isherwood "Charles Isherwood") described it in _The New York Times_ as "a full-scale reimagining" of the musical that involved "the addition and subtraction of several songs ..., the reordering of others", and new dialogue contributed by Condon.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-25) That production received excellent reviews when it moved to Broadway in the fall, but it proved a failure at the box office and closed after just seven weeks.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-26)
In 2015, Condon directed _[Mr. Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_Holmes "Mr. Holmes")_ starring [Ian McKellen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_McKellen "Ian McKellen"). Condon noted its similarity to _Gods and Monsters_, not only because of its lead actor but because "[b]oth movies are about aging and mortality. You have a celebrated man facing the decline of his public image."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-27)

Condon directed the 2017 [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures")'s [live action film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_and_the_Beast_(2017_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)"), [based on](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_remakes_and_adaptations_of_Disney_animated_films "List of remakes and adaptations of Disney animated films") the animated 1991 film _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(1991\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (1991 film)")_, starring [Emma Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Watson "Emma Watson") and [Dan Stevens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Stevens "Dan Stevens").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-CondonDisneylive-actionBeautyandtheBeast-1) A few weeks before the film's scheduled release on March 17, 2017, Condon announced that one character, LeFou, has "a nice, exclusively gay moment", which resulted in an "internet meltdown" of contrasting support and condemnation.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-28)
He co-authored the screenplay for _[The Greatest Showman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Greatest\_Showman "The Greatest Showman")_, a biography of [P.T. Barnum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P.T._Barnum "P.T. Barnum"), starring [Hugh Jackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Jackman "Hugh Jackman") and released in December 2017. He rewrote the draft of co-author [Jenny Bicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenny_Bicks "Jenny Bicks").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-29)

In October 2017, Condon postponed pre-production of a remake of _[Bride of Frankenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bride\_of\_Frankenstein#Remake\_attempts "Bride of Frankenstein")_ for [Universal Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures"). _[Deadline Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline\_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")_ reported that Condon and [David Koepp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koepp "David Koepp") wanted to rework the script.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-30)
Condon is a member of the Independent Feature Projects (IFP) in Los Angeles, a non-profit organization which supports independent films, as well as the Independent Writers Steering Committee, which was initiated by the Writers Guild of America (WGA).
In July 2021, Condon signed on to direct a _[Guys and Dolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guys\_and\_Dolls "Guys and Dolls")_ movie adaptation by [TriStar Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TriStar_Pictures "TriStar Pictures") but left the project in 2023 and was replaced by _Chicago_ director [Rob Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Marshall "Rob Marshall").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-31) That same year, he co-produced the [live stage filming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_from_Away_(film) "Come from Away (film)") of the Broadway production of _[Come from Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come\_from\_Away "Come from Away")_, which was released to streaming on [Apple TV+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV+ "Apple TV+").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-32)

In December 2023, it was announced that Condon would write and direct a [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(2025_film) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (2025 film)") of the [musical version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(musical) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (musical)") of _[Kiss of the Spider Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss\_of\_the\_Spider\_Woman\_(novel) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (novel)")_, with [Jennifer Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lopez "Jennifer Lopez") attached to star and co-executive produce.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-33)
In July 2026, it was revealed that Condon was filming his next film, _The Road Home_, in South Africa. It is about [Hugh Masekela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Masekela "Hugh Masekela") and the conflict he faced from recording with [Paul Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Simon "Paul Simon") during [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-34)
Condon is [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-35) He is in a long-term relationship with Jack Morrissey.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-budget-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-37)

His directorial debut was _[Sister, Sister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister,\_Sister\_(1987\_film) "Sister, Sister (1987 film)")_ (1987), an eerie [Southern Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Gothic "Southern Gothic") mystery starring [Eric Stoltz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Stoltz "Eric Stoltz") and [Jennifer Jason Leigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Jason_Leigh "Jennifer Jason Leigh"). texts.3: _**Kinsey**_ is a 2004 American [biographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film")[drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)") written and directed by [Bill Condon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon "Bill Condon").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_(film)#cite_note-4) It describes the life of [Alfred Charles Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey "Alfred Kinsey") (played by [Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson")), a pioneer in the area of [sexology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexology "Sexology"). His 1948 publication, _Sexual Behavior in the Human Male_ (the first of the [Kinsey Reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_Reports "Kinsey Reports")) was one of the first recorded works that tried to scientifically address and investigate [sexual behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_sexual_activity "Human sexual activity") in humans. The film also stars [Laura Linney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Linney "Laura Linney") (in a performance nominated for the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress")), [Chris O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_O'Donnell "Chris O'Donnell"), [Peter Sarsgaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Sarsgaard "Peter Sarsgaard"), [Timothy Hutton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Hutton "Timothy Hutton"), [John Lithgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lithgow "John Lithgow"), [Tim Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Curry "Tim Curry"), [Oliver Platt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Platt "Oliver Platt"), and [Dylan Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Baker "Dylan Baker").
texts.4:
_Kinsey_ premiered at [Telluride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telluride_Film_Festival "Telluride Film Festival") on September 4, 2004 before being released by [Fox Searchlight Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Searchlight_Pictures "Fox Searchlight Pictures") in the United States on November 12, 2004. The film received positive reviews from critics and grossed $16.9 million against an $11 million budget.
Professor [Alfred Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey "Alfred Kinsey") is interviewed about his sexual history. Interspersed with the interview are flashbacks from his childhood and young-adulthood. The early years show his father, a [lay minister of the Methodist church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodist_local_preacher "Methodist local preacher"), denouncing modern inventions as leading to sexual sin, then in early adolescence, humiliating Kinsey in a store by denouncing its keeper for showing him cigarettes, while his adolescence shows his experiences as a [Boy Scout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Scouts_(Boy_Scouts_of_America) "Boy Scouts (Boy Scouts of America)") and a late teenage scene shows Kinsey disappointing his father by his chosen vocational intentions. The adult Kinsey teaches at [Indiana University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_University_Bloomington "Indiana University Bloomington") as a professor of biology lecturing on [gall wasps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gall_wasp "Gall wasp").
Kinsey falls in love with a student in his class, whom he calls [Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clara_McMillen "Clara McMillen"), and marries her. Consummation of their marriage is difficult at first, because of a medical problem Mac has that is fixed easily with minor surgery. At the university, Professor Kinsey, who is affectionately called "Prok" by his graduate students, meets with them after hours to offer individual sexual advice.
texts.5:
At a book party celebrating Kinsey's latest publication on gall wasps, Kinsey approaches the [dean of students](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_of_students "Dean of students") about an open-forum [sex education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_education "Sex education") course as opposed to the anti-sex propaganda taught in a general [health education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_education "Health education") class. It is approved, but on the grounds that it is open only to teachers, graduate or senior students, and married students. Kinsey begins teaching the sex course to a packed auditorium.
Kinsey continues answering students' questions in personal meetings but his answers are severely limited by the paucity of scientific data about human sexual behavior. This leads Kinsey to pass out questionnaires in his sexual education class from which he learns of the enormous disparity between what society had assumed people do and what their actual practices are. After securing financial support from the [Rockefeller Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Foundation "Rockefeller Foundation"), Kinsey and his research assistants, including his closest assistant, [Clyde Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Martin "Clyde Martin"), travel the country, interviewing subjects about their sexual histories.
As time progresses Kinsey realizes that sexuality within humans, including himself, is a lot more varied than was originally thought. The range of expression he creates becomes known as the [Kinsey scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey_scale "Kinsey scale"), which ranks overall sexuality from completely [heterosexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterosexual "Heterosexual") to completely [homosexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexual "Homosexual").

texts.2: **William Condon** (born October 22, 1955) is an American director and screenwriter. Condon is known for writing and/or directing numerous successful and acclaimed films including _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_, _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_1 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1")_, _[Part 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Twilight\_Saga:\_Breaking\_Dawn\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_2 "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2")_, and _[Beauty and the Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_and\_the\_Beast\_(2017\_film) "Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-CondonDisneylive-actionBeautyandtheBeast-1) He has received two nominations for the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay"), _Gods and Monsters_ and _Chicago_, winning for the former.
texts.5:
Condon emerged a few years later directing a series of made-for-TV thrillers, including _[Murder 101](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder\_101\_(1991\_film) "Murder 101 (1991 film)")_ (1991), which earned Condon and co-writer Roy Johansen a 1992 [Edgar Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Award "Edgar Award") for their screenplay.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-mysterynet-11) During this period he also wrote the screenplay for the thriller _[F/X2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/X2 "F/X2")_ (1991), which was directed by Australian director [Richard Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Franklin_(director) "Richard Franklin (director)").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-12)
In 1994, he directed the television movie _[The Man Who Wouldn't Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Man\_Who\_Wouldn't\_Die\_(1995\_film) "The Man Who Wouldn't Die (1995 film)"),_ which was met with mixed reviews.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-13) He directed _[Candyman: Farewell to the Flesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candyman:\_Farewell\_to\_the\_Flesh "Candyman: Farewell to the Flesh")_ (1995), a sequel to [Bernard Rose's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Rose_(director) "Bernard Rose (director)") 1992 horror film. It was a critical and commercial failure.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-14) Reminded years later of this phase of his career, Condon said: "It's hard to be lower on the totem pole than being the director for a sequel to a horror movie."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-columbiacollege-4)
texts.6: Condon wrote and directed _[Gods and Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods\_and\_Monsters\_(film) "Gods and Monsters (film)")_ (1998), which was based on a novel by [Christopher Bram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Bram "Christopher Bram"). His screenplay won the [Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Writing_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Writing Adapted Screenplay"). _The New York Times_ said Condon "may have been the most stunned person at the Academy Awards when his name was announced as the winner for the best adapted screenplay. He has struggled for years in Hollywood as a screenwriter and journalist and is unaccustomed to the hoopla that is now around him."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-15) He was nominated for the same award for his screenplay for _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(2002\_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")_, based on the Broadway musical of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_(musical) "Chicago (musical)").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-16) He received a second Edgar Award for his _Chicago_ screenplay as well.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-17)
texts.7:
In 2004 he wrote and directed the film _[Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinsey\_(film) "Kinsey (film)")_, chronicling the life of the controversial sex researcher [Alfred Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Kinsey "Alfred Kinsey"). In _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, [A.O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.O._Scott "A.O. Scott") wrote that "Bill Condon's smart, stirring [film] has a lot to say on the subject of sex, which it treats with sobriety, sensitivity and a welcome measure of humor." He continued: "I can't think of another movie that has dealt with sex so knowledgeably and, at the same time, made the pursuit of knowledge seem so sexy. There are some explicit images and provocative scenes, but it is your intellect that is most likely to be aroused.... Mr. Condon's great achievement is to turn Kinsey's complicated and controversial career into a grand intellectual drama."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-18)
In 2005, he received the [Stephen F. Kolzak Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD_Media_Awards "GLAAD Media Awards") at the [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD "GLAAD") Media Awards.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-19)
Condon wrote the screenplay for and directed _[Dreamgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls\_(film) "Dreamgirls (film)")_, an adaptation of the acclaimed Broadway musical of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamgirls "Dreamgirls"). It was released in December 2006. Condon received [Directors Guild of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_America "Directors Guild of America") and [Broadcast Film Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_Film_Critics_Association "Broadcast Film Critics Association") nominations for directing. The film was nominated for eight Academy Awards in six categories.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-20)
texts.8:
Condon was executive producer of the [81st Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards") television broadcast that aired on February 22, 2009, working with producer [Laurence Mark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Mark "Laurence Mark").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-21)
Condon directed both parts of _[The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaking\_Dawn\_(disambiguation) "Breaking Dawn (disambiguation)")_ (2011 and 2012), adapted from the fourth and final novel in _[The Twilight Saga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_(novel\_series) "Twilight (novel series)")_ by [Stephenie Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephenie_Meyer "Stephenie Meyer"). He was twice nominated for a [Razzie for Worst Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Award_for_Worst_Director "Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Director") for these films, winning for _Part 2_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-22)
Condon directed _[The Fifth Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fifth\_Estate\_(film) "The Fifth Estate (film)")_ (2013), a thriller about [WikiLeaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks "WikiLeaks") starring [Benedict Cumberbatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_Cumberbatch "Benedict Cumberbatch"). He said he chose the project for a change of pace and liked its non-ideological approach to a very complex subject. He saw it "in the great tradition of journalistic thrillers".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-23) It received mixed responses from critics and underperformed at the box office.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-24)
texts.9:
In late 2013, he directed a revised version of the 1997 stage musical _[Side Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side\_Show\_(musical) "Side Show (musical)")_ at the [La Jolla Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Jolla_Playhouse "La Jolla Playhouse"). A production of this revision played in June and July 2014 at the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center"). [Charles Isherwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Isherwood "Charles Isherwood") described it in _The New York Times_ as "a full-scale reimagining" of the musical that involved "the addition and subtraction of several songs ..., the reordering of others", and new dialogue contributed by Condon.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-25) That production received excellent reviews when it moved to Broadway in the fall, but it proved a failure at the box office and closed after just seven weeks.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-26)
In 2015, Condon directed _[Mr. Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_Holmes "Mr. Holmes")_ starring [Ian McKellen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_McKellen "Ian McKellen"). Condon noted its similarity to _Gods and Monsters_, not only because of its lead actor but because "[b]oth movies are about aging and mortality. You have a celebrated man facing the decline of his public image."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-27)
texts.12:
In December 2023, it was announced that Condon would write and direct a [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(2025_film) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (2025 film)") of the [musical version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_the_Spider_Woman_(musical) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (musical)") of _[Kiss of the Spider Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss\_of\_the\_Spider\_Woman\_(novel) "Kiss of the Spider Woman (novel)")_, with [Jennifer Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lopez "Jennifer Lopez") attached to star and co-executive produce.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-33)
In July 2026, it was revealed that Condon was filming his next film, _The Road Home_, in South Africa. It is about [Hugh Masekela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Masekela "Hugh Masekela") and the conflict he faced from recording with [Paul Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Simon "Paul Simon") during [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-34)
Condon is [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-35) He is in a long-term relationship with Jack Morrissey.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-budget-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Condon#cite_note-37)
